name: Chavismo
summary: Chavismo is the left-populist, Bolivarian movement built around Hugo Chávez and continued by Nicolás Maduro. It combines nationalism, Latin American integration and anti-imperialism with 'socialism of the 21st century': oil-funded social missions, nationalization, price controls and a communal state of participatory bodies, set against an 'oligarchy' and neoliberalism. It accepts private property alongside social property, and it is socially conservative on abortion and marriage.
scope: The mainstream Chavista project: Hugo Chavez's movement as the scholars Smilde and Azzellini define it ('left populist', 'Revolutionary Bolivarianism', socialism as its main symbolic discourse from 2005). Its own texts used are the 1999 Constitution, the Programa de la Patria (2013-2019), Chavez's 2012 Golpe de Timon and his UN speeches; the record is read through scholars such as Smilde and Wilpert. It excludes the pragmatic reprivatizing turn after Chavez, other Bolivarian-family movements and the wider pan-Latin socialism of the 21st century.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Art. 328 organises a National Armed Force 'to guarantee the independence and sovereignty of the Nation'.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Art. 318 gives the Venezuelan Central Bank exclusive monetary competence.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Art. 21: 'No titles of nobility or hereditary distinctions shall be recognized'.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Art. 316 builds the tax system on a fair distribution of public burdens by ability to pay with progressive taxation.

abolish-ip.rationale: Art. 98 recognises and protects intellectual property rights in scientific, literary and artistic works, inventions and patents.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Art. 332 provides for national police and other security bodies.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Arts. 87-91 secure wages, a vital minimum salary and the right to a share of profits for employees.

abortion-legal.rationale: Art. 76 protects maternity from conception, and the same sub-commission opposes reform of the Criminal Code's abortion stance, which has barely changed under chavismo.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Art. 115 guarantees property and Art. 307 says farmers are entitled to own land and the State protects private and associative property.

allow-dual-citizenship.rationale: Art. 34: 'The Venezuelan nationality is not lost upon electing or acquiring another nationality'.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Art. 59 guarantees every person the right to profess a religious faith and express beliefs.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Art. 187 gives the National Assembly the power to approve the Law of the Budget of the State.

civilizational-union.rationale: Art. 153 commits the Republic to promote Latin American and Caribbean integration toward a 'community of nations'.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Art. 152 governs foreign relations by equality between States and free self-determination.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Art. 96 guarantees voluntary collective bargaining and collective agreements in the public and private sectors.

common-currency.rationale: Art. 318 provides for a common currency should one be instituted within Latin American integration.

conscription.rationale: Art. 134 makes civil or military service a duty but states 'No one shall be subjected to forcible recruitment'.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Art. 5: sovereignty resides non-delegably in the people.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Art. 347: 'The original constituent power rests with the people', exercised by calling a National Constituent Assembly, and Art. 348 lets citizens initiate it.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Chavez's Golpe de Timon demands the creation of communes and the Law of the Communal Economy as the core of the new state.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Art. 100 recognises 'intercultural relations under the principle of equality of cultures'.

death-penalty.rationale: Art. 43: 'No law shall provide for the death penalty and no authority shall apply the same'.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Art. 87 guarantees measures so everyone can obtain productive work providing 'a dignified and decorous living', and Art. 91 a salary sufficient for basic needs.

decide-locally.rationale: Art. 158 makes decentralization a national policy to 'bring power closer to the people', and Chavez's 2012 Golpe de Timon demands that communes be built as the base of the state.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Art. 152 governs foreign relations by independence and equality between States.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Art. 228: the President is elected by universal suffrage by direct and secret ballot.

direct-votes.rationale: Arts. 70-74 give citizens consultative, recall, approving and abrogatory referendums on laws and treaties, which Wilpert lists among constitutionally guaranteed participation rights.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Art. 5 places sovereignty in the people.

dominated-front.rationale: The Programa de la Patria names ALBA and Petrocaribe as the instruments of a new multipolar geopolitics against imperial domination, and Chavez at the UN called for a front of developing countries.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Art. 228 fills the presidency by direct popular election, Art. 21 recognises no hereditary distinctions.

elective-rulers.rationale: Art. 228 has the people elect the President directly, and Art. 6 calls government 'elective'.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Art. 21: 'All persons are equal before the law'.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Preamble reshapes the Republic as a 'multiethnic and multicultural society', and Art. 100 holds an 'equality of cultures'.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Art. 302 keeps the State owner of PDVSA, and the Programa de la Patria sets oil-sector production and storage targets; Smilde describes an economy and state revenue built on oil.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Art. 43 declares the right to life inviolable and bars the death penalty.

force-without-un.rationale: Art. 152 binds foreign policy to non-intervention and peaceful resolution of conflicts, and Chavez told the UN the US 'wants to impose its system of exploitation and pillage and its hegemony through war'.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Art. 64 extends the vote in state, municipal and parish elections to foreign residents over 18 with more than ten years of residence.

free-public-college.rationale: Art. 103: 'Education offered at State institutions is free of charge up to the undergraduate university level'.

free-trade.rationale: The Programa de la Patria presents ALBA and Petrocaribe as an alternative to the existing order and denounces the 'savage and destructive' capitalist system; Chavez at the UN called the neoliberal model a cause of poverty.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Art. 21 states 'No discrimination based on race, sex, creed or social standing shall be permitted' and applies it generally.

future-generations.rationale: Art. 127: 'It is the right and duty of each generation to protect and maintain the environment for its own benefit and that of the world of the future'.

gradual-change.rationale: Chavismo names itself the Bolivarian Revolution and Chavez came to prominence in the 1992 uprising; scholars describe a movement for social transformation, not stepwise reform.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Art. 236 makes the President Commander in Chief with 'supreme hierarchical authority' over the armed forces.

head-of-state-dissolves-parliament.rationale: Art. 236 lets the President dissolve the National Assembly in the cases the Constitution contemplates, and Art. 240 authorizes it after the third removal of an Executive Vice-President in one term.

indigenous-internal-justice.rationale: Art. 260: native authorities may apply their own justice 'based on their ancestral traditions' to their members.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Arts. 119-120 recognise native peoples' own social, political and economic organisation and their collective rights to their ancestral lands.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Art. 86 makes social security a 'nonprofit public service' the State guarantees.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Arts. 119-124 give native peoples collective rights and Art. 124 collective intellectual property in their knowledge.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Art. 77 founds marriage on free consent and equal rights of the spouses.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Art. 152 governs foreign relations by non-intervention in states' internal affairs.

job-guarantee.rationale: Art. 87: 'The State guarantees the adoption of the necessary measures so that every person shall be able to obtain productive work'.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: Art. 87: 'All persons have the right and duty to work'.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Art. 304 makes all waters public domain and Art. 84 keeps the health system public.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Art. 33 requires ten years of uninterrupted residence for a naturalization letter, though shorter terms apply to some groups such as spouses (five years).

mandatory-environmental-reporting.rationale: Art. 129 requires environmental and socio-cultural impact studies before activities capable of damaging ecosystems.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Chavez told the UN that the 'capitalist neo-liberal model ... creates poverty', and the Programa de la Patria sets as its objective the destruction of 'savage capitalism' and social property over the basic means of production; in practice the government set price controls on about half of all goods.

minority-language-support.rationale: Art. 9 gives native languages official status for native peoples and requires their use be respected throughout the territory.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Art. 84 makes health a State-run public system and bars privatising public health assets.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Art. 1 and Art. 5 found the Republic on popular sovereignty, Art. 21 forbids titles of nobility and hereditary distinctions.

multipolar-world.rationale: The Programa de la Patria makes contributing to a multipolar international geopolitics a historic objective, and Chavez told the UN to end the US veto and expand the Security Council with developing states.

national-church-status.rationale: Art. 59 guarantees freedom of religion and the autonomy and independence of religious confessions and churches.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Arts. 119-124 recognise native peoples' own social, political, economic and cultural organisation, customs and languages.

national-resource-control.rationale: Art. 12: mineral and hydrocarbon deposits are property of the Republic, 'inalienable and not transferable'; Art. 302 reserves the petroleum industry to the State.

national-self-determination.rationale: Art. 1 declares independence and national self-determination 'unrenounceable rights of the Nation', and Art. 152 commits foreign policy to free self-determination.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Art. 6 makes government 'elective' and Art. 63 vests suffrage in free, universal, direct and secret elections.

one-party-rule.rationale: Art. 6 calls government 'pluralist' and Art. 67 gives all citizens the right to associate in political parties; Wilpert and Smilde record competitive elections alongside dominance by the movement's party.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Art. 62 gives all citizens the right to participate in public affairs directly, and calls the people's participation 'the necessary way' to complete development.

party-commands-army.rationale: Art. 328 describes the National Armed Forces as 'with no political orientation'.

party-controls-media.rationale: Smilde records that after the private media's role in the 2002 coup the government 'strengthened its control over media' by law and by expanding state media.

person-over-state.rationale: Art. 3 makes the protection and development of the person and respect for human dignity the essential purposes of the State.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Smilde records that the government 'progressively instituted price controls on about half of all goods and services'.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Programa de la Patria makes the 'supreme social happiness of the people' its aim and builds the social missions, which Wilpert describes as the core of the project.

production-for-use.rationale: The Programa de la Patria calls for social property over the basic means of production and Chavez's Golpe de Timon calls to graft 'social property, the socialist spirit' along the production chain.

property-franchise.rationale: Art. 63 sets only age and nationality as conditions for voting; none of wealth or property.

property-fundamental.rationale: Art. 115 guarantees the right of property but subjects it to restrictions 'in the service of the public or general interest' and allows expropriation for social interest; the government used expropriation widely.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Art. 115 subjects property to contributions, restrictions and obligations in the service of the general interest.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Art. 143: citizens 'have access to administrative files and records', subject to limits for security and privacy.

public-ownership.rationale: Art. 302 reserves the petroleum industry and other strategic industries to the State; scholars record expropriations of steel, cement and telecommunications firms and an emphasis on 'expanded state management/ownership'.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Art. 21 forbids discrimination based on race.

racial-franchise.rationale: Art. 63 gives the vote to every Venezuelan over 18 with no condition of race or origin.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Art. 21 forbids any discrimination based on race, sex, creed or social standing.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Art. 91 guarantees every worker a salary sufficient to live with dignity and cover basic needs, and a vital minimum salary adjusted each year with the cost of a basic market basket as a reference.

recall-officials.rationale: Art. 72 makes all elected offices revocable by referendum, and Art. 6 describes government as one 'with revocable mandates'.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Art. 72 lets voters recall any elected office by referendum after the midpoint of its term, and Art. 6 describes 'revocable mandates'.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The government set price controls on about half of all goods and services and expropriated firms, per Smilde.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Art. 21 forbids discrimination based on race and creed, and the Preamble founds a multiethnic society.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Art. 59 guarantees every person the right to profess a religious faith and express beliefs.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Art. 97 guarantees all workers in the public and private sectors the right to strike.

right-to-secede.rationale: Art. 4 states territorial integrity as a governing principle, Art. 13 bars any transfer of territory, and Art. 126 calls the Venezuelan people 'one, sovereign and indivisible'.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Art. 77 protects marriage and defines stable unions as between a man and a woman; a National Assembly sub-commission under chavismo opposes any legislative initiative approving gay marriage.

second-chamber.rationale: Art. 186 constitutes a single National Assembly of deputies, with no second chamber.

separated-powers.rationale: Art. 136 divides national public power into legislative, executive, judicial, citizen and electoral branches, which 'shall cooperate with one another'.

single-official-language.rationale: Art. 9 makes Spanish official but gives native languages official status for native peoples.

socialized-markets.rationale: Wilpert records the government promoting cooperatives and 'state, collective, or mixed ownership' enterprises with preferential credit, alongside a market economy.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Art. 7: 'All persons and organs exercising Public Power are subject to this Constitution'.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Art. 324: 'Only the State shall be permitted to possess and use weapons of war'.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Art. 302 reserves strategic industries to the State and Art. 112 commits the State to plan economic development; Smilde lists 'greater state control over the economy' among the main ideas of the transition to socialism.

state-harmful.rationale: Art. 2 constitutes Venezuela as a 'Democratic and Social State of Law and Justice'; the movement's programme builds a state, not its abolition.

taxation-theft.rationale: Art. 133: 'Everyone has the duty to contribute toward public expenditures by paying such taxes'.

term-limits.rationale: Art. 230 as revised in 2009 lets the President be re-elected with no limit on terms.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Art. 46: 'No person shall be subjected to penalties, tortures, cruelty, inhuman or degrading treatment'.

traditional-family.rationale: Art. 75 protects the family as a natural association and Art. 76 protects maternity and paternity.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Art. 83 makes health a fundamental social right the State guarantees, and Art. 84 creates a national public health system governed by 'gratuity, universality, completeness, fairness'.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Art. 230 as revised in 2009: 'The presidential term is of six years. The President ... may be re-elected', with no limit on the number of terms.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: Art. 63 sets the voting age at 18.

women-suffrage.rationale: Art. 63 gives every Venezuelan over 18 the vote, and Art. 21 forbids discrimination based on sex.

worker-ownership.rationale: Chavez told the UN: 'Why should there just be one or two capitalists exploiting a lot of people?' and proposed giving a factory to its workers; Wilpert records cooperatives rising from about 800 to over 100,000 and co-management experiments.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Wilpert records co-management experiments in state firms such as CADAFE and Alcasa.

missingStatements.text: A president should be allowed to stand for re-election without limit.
missingStatements.rationale: Art. 230 as revised in 2009 lets the President be re-elected with no limit on terms; the 2009 referendum approved the change.

missingStatements.text: Elected officials, including the president, should be removable by a recall referendum during their term.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 72 makes all elected offices revocable by referendum, and Article 6 calls government one with 'revocable mandates'.

notes: Themes searched: economy and ownership, welfare and labour, property, democracy and participation, institutions, sovereignty and foreign policy, the UN, religion and family, race and indigenous peoples, environment, the armed forces and media. Almost every answer now rests on an article of the Constitution or on a scholar's account of the record; Wikipedia-based answers from the earlier pass were nulled where no primary or scholarly source states the position. Chavez's own texts (Programa de la Patria, Golpe de Timon, UN speeches) were read for economic and international themes; the scanned Programa extracts are garbled by columns, so answers on it are medium. Scholarly sources that were saved but yielded no direct statements (Tendencias, Polis, Green Left) are not cited. Positions are those of the Chavez-era mainstream; Madurismo is harder-line and Delcismo more pragmatic on markets.

aliases.name: chavista
aliases.quote: Nicolás Maduro’s chavista government has ceased to be popular, although chavismo more broadly and its iconic figure still are.

keyFigures.role: Founder and leader of the Bolivarian Revolution and president 1999-2013
keyFigures.quote: Chavismo is a left populist movement that adopted socialism as its main symbolic discourse during the presidency of Hugo Chávez Frías.
